Hi Ana — thanks for the clear asks.

Quick answer: we can produce a 6-week onramp MAP for a first tranche of ~120 H100-equivalent GPUs with staged deliveries and a predictable SLA for Dedicated. For a 200–400 GPU target we usually recommend a 3-tranche plan (120 -> +80 -> +200 backfill) over 10–14 weeks depending on region and preferred hardware vendor.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll draft a compact MAP (milestones + acceptance criteria) and a one-page eval plan showing SOC2 artifacts, perf test harness, and pass/fail thresholds.
- Marissa will model tranche sizing and expected per-token cost delta by quantization profile.
- Ben will confirm procurement windows against our capacity pipeline and any preferred fulfillment lanes.

Marissa/Ben/Laura — looping you in to own the attachments and timeline. Can we aim to share a draft MAP + evaluation PDF by EOD Thursday (5/21)? Ana — if that works, I’ll send the MAP with two schedule options (accelerated vs. conservative).

Best,
Sean

Subject: DRAFT MAP + evaluation plan for Nexera (attached)

Ana / team — attaching the draft materials as discussed. Highlights below:

Attachments: MAP_Nexera_v1.xlsx (MAP milestones + owner matrix), Nexera_eval_plan_v1.pdf (one-page eval + SOC2 checklist)

Key assumptions called out in the MAP:
- Target first tranche: 120 H100-eq (wk0–wk6), acceptance window: perf tests + KV cache validation + SOC2 doc delivery.
- Second tranche: +80 H100-eq (wk7–wk10) contingent on successful acceptance and committed spend.
- Final tranche: +200 H100-eq (wk11–wk16) dependent on procurement lead-time confirmation and capacity locks.
- Staging buffer: we recommend a 10% buffer on top of nominal tranche to cover early peak.

Procurement/lead time notes (from Ben):
- Current estimated lead times for Dedicated capacity in us-west: 8–10 weeks for new H100-equivalent pools if we trigger reserved capacity now; 12–14 weeks in constrained periods.
- Private on-prem installs follow a different cadence — hardware procurement + on-site staging typically add 6–8 weeks to the Dedicated timeline.

We also included a compact acceptance checklist: throughput SLO (p99 generation <= 320ms for 2k tokens), end-to-end latency SLA, and a perf regression guardrail tied back to baseline model.

Let us know which schedule you prefer (Option A accelerated: compress 2nd tranche into wk5–wk9; Option B conservative: spread to wk7–wk12). We can turn the spreadsheet into a mutual action tracker and a DocuSign when you’re ready.

—Marissa

Ana — quick answers below and I attached a short delta summary (exported table) to the MAP spreadsheet: 

1) Private on-prem responsibilities: customer provides rack space, local networking, power provisioning, and physical install scheduling. Redwood provides the inference runtime, orchestration software, and integration support for KMS/HSM. We’ll mark acceptance checkpoints where customer signs off on performance & security artifacts.

2) P&L delta: accelerated path increases committed capacity costs by ~14% in the first 3 months vs conservative path due to front-loaded tranche reservation, but reduces expected unit cost after wk12 by ~22% because of higher utilization. See 'cost_delta' tab in MAP_Nexera_v1.xlsx.

I’ve also confirmed tentative Reserved capacity windows for us-west: if we lock tranche 1 by 6/02 we can target provisioning start wk3 (mid-June) and a go-live acceptance window ending wk8. Without a lock until 6/18 we move 4–6 weeks later due to queueing.

I’ll upload the MAP to the deal record and share a DocuSign statement once Ana confirms Option A or B.
